name: Next.js image optimizer dangerouslyAllowSVG enabled
attack_scenario: attacker uploads an SVG containing <script>fetch('/api',...)</script>, requests it via /_next/image, and the optimizer serves it same-origin so the script runs in a victim's session
negative_test_hint: upload an SVG containing "<script>alert(1)</script>" and request it through the image optimizer, asserting it is refused or served under a script-blocking CSP

exemplar.compliant: module.exports = { images: { contentDispositionType: 'attachment', contentSecurityPolicy: "default-src 'none'; script-src 'none'; sandbox;" } };
exemplar.explanation: Next.js disables SVG through next/image by default because SVGs can embed <script>. dangerouslyAllowSVG:true serves attacker-supplied SVGs from the app origin, and without a strict CSP this is stored XSS.
